title: Vyapam. The exam-and-jobs racket with a body count

human.v: Thousands of rigged medical seats and government jobs; 40+ accused and witnesses reportedly dead in suspicious circumstances

cost.v: A decade of poisoned admissions and recruitment in Madhya Pradesh

what: A vast racket in Madhya Pradesh's professional examinations board rigged medical-college admissions and government recruitment through impersonation and bribery, on an industrial scale.
dodge: As the net widened, an unusually long list of accused and witnesses turned up dead. The state government fought a CBI probe until the High Court forced one in 2015. Not one senior political figure was held to account for a fraud that ran for years under the state's own board, and the deaths were quietly filed away.
pos: The state said the arrests and the later CBI probe proved the system worked, and denied any cover-up.
alleg: The count and cause of the associated deaths are contested and largely unproven; several were officially recorded as natural causes or accidents.
alt: An independent probe from the first day, real protection for witnesses, and political ownership of a scam that festered for years.

title: Demonetisation. Savings voided overnight

human.v: Cash-wage workers, farmers and traders across the country; 100+ deaths reported in queues and in the distress that followed

cost.v: ~₹1.5 to 2 lakh cr est. output loss; 99.3% of the banned notes came back to the RBI

what: ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes, about 86 percent of cash in circulation, were voided with four hours of notice to kill black money, counterfeits and terror funding.
dodge: The RBI later reported almost all the cash returned, so almost no unaccounted wealth was destroyed. No one resigned. No review admitted error. The stated aim simply shifted from black money to digitisation once the first claim collapsed. The suffering was inflicted on the cash-poor; the reckoning was inflicted on nobody.
pos: The government maintains it widened the tax base and accelerated digital payments.
alt: An honest cost-benefit review against the original goals, and a hunt for black money where it actually sits, in benami property, shell firms and opaque political funding, not in a daily-wager's pocket.

title: GST. Compliance chaos loaded onto the small

human.v: Millions of small firms and traders squeezed by filing burden and blocked cash flow

cost.v: Delayed state compensation ran into tens of thousands of crore

what: A single indirect tax replaced a tangle of central and state levies. A genuine reform, launched with too many slabs, endless rule changes and a portal that buckled.
dodge: The cost of a rushed launch was dumped on small businesses, and the states' promised compensation arrived late and grudgingly. The rules were patched again and again, but the disruption was never once owned as a failure of preparation.

ministers.r: Finance Minister and GST Council chair

pos: The government credits GST with ending tax-on-tax and building one national market.
alt: Fewer slabs, a stable rulebook, a tested IT backbone before launch, a real small-business threshold, and compensation paid on time.

title: Electoral bonds. The anonymous money machine

human.v: Every voter, stripped of the right to know who funds power

cost.v: ₹12,146 cr encashed in total; the ruling BJP took ~₹6,000 cr+, more than the next six parties combined

what: A scheme that let donors hand unlimited, publicly anonymous sums to parties through the state-owned SBI, while scrapping the cap on corporate donations.
dodge: Sold as transparency, it delivered secrecy for the public and visibility for whoever controlled the state bank. When the Supreme Court forced disclosure, the numbers confirmed the ruling party as the runaway top beneficiary. The Court struck the scheme down as unconstitutional in 2024. For the years of lopsided, hidden money it enabled, nobody was ever held to account.
pos: The government argued the scheme moved donations into banking channels and protected donor privacy.
alleg: Reporting and the opposition alleged patterns linking bond purchases to contracts and to the timing of agency raids on donors. These are contested allegations; the Court ruled on constitutionality, not on any specific quid pro quo.
alt: Full public disclosure of every donor, a firm corporate cap, a bar on shell and loss-making donors, and a move to capped small-donor or state funding.

sources.label: BJP got more than next 6 combined

title: Rafale. The pricing and offset row

human.v: No direct death toll. The stake is public trust in defence spending.

cost.v: Opposition alleged a far higher per-jet price than the earlier negotiation (contested)

what: India agreed to buy 36 Rafale fighter jets from France in a government-to-government deal, dropping an earlier plan to buy more jets with local manufacture.
dodge: When the opposition alleged the per-jet price was inflated and questioned an offset contract routed to a newly formed private firm, the government withheld the pricing on security grounds and refused a Joint Parliamentary Committee. The absence of any independent scrutiny, not a proven crime, is the accountability gap.
pos: The government denied any irregularity; the Supreme Court declined to order an investigation and dismissed review petitions.
alleg: The price and offset claims are opposition allegations the courts did not uphold. No wrongdoing was established; the criticism is of secrecy and the refusal of a JPC.
alt: An independent audit trail and parliamentary oversight of pricing on mega defence deals, protecting real secrets without shielding the whole deal from scrutiny.

title: Pulwama. 40 troopers dead, the questions buried

human.v: 40 CRPF personnel killed when a suicide bomber rammed their convoy

cost.v: A catastrophic intelligence and security failure on a known-sensitive highway

what: A vehicle packed with explosives struck a CRPF convoy in Pulwama, Kashmir, killing 40 personnel in the deadliest attack on Indian forces in the region in decades.
dodge: No findings on the security lapse were ever made public. The then Governor of J&K, Satya Pal Malik, later stated openly that there had been grave lapses, including a denied request to airlift the convoy, and said he was told at the highest level to keep quiet because the blame would be placed on Pakistan. Those claims were never independently examined. Forty dead troopers got a war of rhetoric, not an inquiry.
pos: The government treated it as terrorism and answered with the Balakot airstrikes; it did not act on Malik's later claims.
alleg: The lapse claims are those of former Governor Satya Pal Malik and remain unexamined by any public inquiry.
alt: An independent, published inquiry into the intelligence and logistics failure. The least owed to 40 dead men and their families.

title: The lockdown migrant exodus. 'No data' on the dead

human.v: 10 million+ displaced; hundreds to 1,000+ estimated deaths on roads and rails; tens of millions of jobs lost

cost.v: Not a rupee in compensation, because the state said it had no data on which to base any

what: A nationwide lockdown announced with four hours of notice stranded migrant workers with no transport, no work and no income, forcing millions to walk home. Many died of exhaustion, accidents and hunger.
dodge: Asked in Parliament how many migrants died and what compensation was owed, the Labour Ministry answered that no such data was maintained, so the question of compensation did not arise. Refusing to count the dead became the very device for owing nothing to the living. It is hard to imagine a colder abdication.

ministers.r: Prime Minister who announced the lockdown

pos: The government said it provided food, ration and Shramik trains to ease migrants' hardship.
alt: Count every death, publish the toll, compensate the families. Build in humane transition time before shutting a nation down.

title: PM CARES. A public fund that hides from the public

human.v: Every taxpayer and donor with a stake in how relief money is spent

cost.v: Thousands of crore in donations, including from state-owned firms; donors and spending undisclosed

what: A trust set up days into the pandemic to collect COVID-relief donations, using the Prime Minister's name, the national emblem and a gov.in domain.
dodge: For all the trappings of the state, the government insists PM CARES is a private trust, so it is not a public authority under RTI and is not audited by the CAG. No citizen can learn who gave, or where the money went. A fund that borrows the state's face while dodging the state's accountability is opacity by design.

ministers.n: Amit Shah, Rajnath Singh, Nirmala Sitharaman

pos: The government says the fund is independently audited and its expenditure summaries are published.
alt: Bring it under RTI and CAG audit and disclose donors and disbursements, the standard for any fund that trades on the nation's name and symbols.

title: Galwan. 20 soldiers dead, and 'no one entered'

human.v: 20 Indian soldiers killed, 70+ injured, the first LAC combat deaths in 45 years

cost.v: Reported loss of patrolling access at several points along the Ladakh LAC

what: Indian and Chinese troops fought hand to hand in the Galwan Valley in Ladakh. Twenty Indian soldiers were killed in the deadliest border clash with China since 1962.
dodge: Days later, the Prime Minister told an all-party meeting that nobody had entered Indian territory and no post had been captured. Critics said it handed Beijing a propaganda gift and contradicted his own government's earlier account. If no one intruded, they asked, where did 20 soldiers die? No accountability followed for the intelligence failure or the lost ground.
pos: The PMO said the remark referred to the situation after the army repelled the transgression, and pointed to disengagement talks.
alt: A straight account to Parliament of what territory was lost and why, an intelligence-failure review, and honesty owed to the dead.

title: Central Vista. A vanity rebuild in a plague year

human.v: A pandemic-era spend while oxygen and vaccines ran short

cost.v: ~₹20,000 cr redevelopment, including a new Parliament (~₹970 cr)

what: The government pressed ahead with a sweeping redevelopment of the capital's central avenue and a new Parliament building through the pandemic, declaring it an essential project.
dodge: As citizens queued for oxygen and hospitals ran dry, thousands of crore went into remaking the seat of power, with the heritage and cost concerns brushed aside and the courts asked to treat it as untouchable. The priorities were never honestly defended to a grieving public.
pos: The government said the old buildings were unfit and outdated and the project would save money over time.
alt: Sequence the spending behind the emergency, publish the full cost and rationale, and let heritage and Parliament oversight run their course.

title: Farm laws. Rammed through, then repealed
stamp: Reversed after a year of protest

human.v: ~700 protesting farmers reported dead over the year-long agitation

cost.v: A year of blockades and lost trade; the dead long unacknowledged

what: Three laws to deregulate farm markets were passed by a contested voice vote amid uproar, with no real consultation of the states (agriculture is largely a state subject) or of farmers.
dodge: Farmers protested for a year over fears for assured procurement, and hundreds died at the protest sites. The government finally repealed all three laws, then framed the retreat as a failure to explain the reform, never as an error of substance or process, and was slow even to acknowledge the dead.
pos: The government said the laws would have let farmers sell anywhere and drawn in investment.
alleg: Farm unions alleged the laws favoured large agri-corporates, a contested political allegation; the repeal followed the protests, not any adjudicated finding.
alt: Legislate farm reform with the states and farmers at the table, put MSP on firmer footing, and pilot changes that can be tested and trusted.

title: Labour codes. Worker protections gutted in silence

human.v: A rising share of the workforce pushed into insecure, easily-terminated contracts

cost.v: Weakened job security and collective bargaining for millions

what: Twenty-nine labour laws were folded into four codes, raising the threshold for firing workers without permission, expanding fixed-term contracts and tightening the rules for legal strikes.
dodge: The codes were passed while much of the opposition was absent or suspended, with almost no debate on provisions that hand bargaining power decisively to employers, and then left in years of limbo through stalled implementation.
pos: The government says the codes simplify compliance, ease business and formalise jobs.
alt: Match any hiring flexibility with portable social security and real unemployment support, agreed through genuine tripartite consultation.

title: COVID second wave. The denial of the oxygen dead

human.v: 3.4 to 4.7 million excess deaths estimated (WHO) against ~0.5 million official, and zero oxygen deaths admitted

cost.v: Families left uncompensated for deaths the state refused to record

what: As the Delta wave overran hospitals, patients died gasping in acute oxygen shortages while families begged for cylinders in the street.
dodge: The government told Parliament that no deaths due to lack of oxygen had been specifically reported by any state, a claim contradicted by hospitals, courts and the media. A parliamentary committee rebuked the ministry for its denial. When the WHO put India's real toll at up to ten times the official count, the government attacked the methodology rather than face the gap. The dead were disowned twice: once in the wards, once in the record.

ministers.r: MoS Health who made the statement

pos: The government said health is a state subject, that states had not reported oxygen-specific deaths, and it disputed the WHO estimate.
alt: Audit the oxygen deaths, publish an honest excess-mortality count, and compensate the families, exactly as the parliamentary committee recommended.

title: Stan Swamy. An 84-year-old dies an undertrial
stamp: Custodial death. Bail refused to the end.

human.v: An 84-year-old priest and tribal-rights activist, dead in custody, never tried, never convicted

cost.v: A chilling message to every ageing or ailing activist facing the UAPA

what: Father Stan Swamy, jailed in the Bhima Koregaon case under the anti-terror UAPA, was denied bail and, at first, even a straw and sipper cup to drink with, and died in custody as an undertrial.
dodge: The state opposed his bail even as his body gave out. No one answered for the death of an octogenarian held for months without trial under a law whose bail bar is almost impossible to clear. This was punishment by process, with the process itself as the sentence.
pos: Agencies maintained the case was a grave national-security matter that followed due legal process.
alt: Humane bail for the old and the sick, a workable UAPA bail standard, and accountability for deaths of undertrials in state custody.

title: Pegasus. Spyware, and a refusal to answer

human.v: Journalists, activists, opposition figures and officials on the alleged target list

cost.v: Not quantified. The damage is to a free press and a fair opposition.

what: A global investigation reported that military-grade Pegasus spyware may have targeted the phones of Indian journalists, activists and opposition politicians.
dodge: Rather than say plainly whether the state had bought or used the spyware, the government neither confirmed nor denied it, and then withheld cooperation from the Supreme Court's own technical committee, which reported it could not get the government to engage. A clean denial was never offered. The question was simply left to rot.
pos: The government dismissed the reporting as an attempt to malign Indian democracy and cited national security.
alleg: Whether the government itself deployed Pegasus remains unconfirmed; the SC panel found malware on some devices but could not conclusively attribute it, partly because of non-cooperation.
alt: Answer under oath, place surveillance under judicial and parliamentary oversight, and legislate warrants and review.

title: Internet shutdowns. Democracy switched off

human.v: Millions cut off from information, income and help during shutdowns; Kashmir endured one of the world's longest

cost.v: Billions of dollars in estimated economic losses over the years

what: India has repeatedly imposed more internet shutdowns than any other country, from the record-length blackout in Jammu and Kashmir after 2019 to routine shutdowns during protests and exams.
dodge: The blackouts are ordered with little transparency and no independent test of necessity, cutting citizens off from banking, medicine, schooling and news, and the human and economic cost is never accounted for or owned.
pos: Authorities cite law and order and the prevention of rumour and violence.
alt: Narrow, time-bound, judicially reviewable shutdowns as a genuine last resort, with published justification and cost.

title: Delhi riots. The dead, and the selective dock

human.v: ~53 killed, most of them Muslim; hundreds injured, thousands displaced

cost.v: Homes, shops and mosques gutted across north-east Delhi

what: Communal violence tore through north-east Delhi over several days in February 2020, killing around 53 people, the majority of them Muslim.
dodge: Rights groups documented police inaction and, in places, complicity, while the state built a sweeping conspiracy case that jailed students and activists under the UAPA for years without trial. Several figures who had made openly inflammatory speeches faced no such action. The prosecution's aim looked less like justice than a message.
pos: Police deny bias and say the investigation followed the evidence of an organised conspiracy.
alleg: The claims of police complicity and one-sided prosecution are contested, advanced by rights groups and the accused and denied by the police; several cases remain in court.
alt: An independent inquiry into the policing, bail and fair trials for undertrials, and even-handed prosecution of incitement whoever spoke it.

title: Hathras. A victim, and a cremation at 2am

human.v: A young Dalit woman dead after an alleged gang rape; her body burned without the family's consent

cost.v: A community's trust in the state, set alight in the dark

what: A 19-year-old Dalit woman died after an alleged gang rape in Hathras, UP. Police cremated her body in the dead of night, without her family present or willing, and officials at first disputed that a rape had occurred.
dodge: A forced night cremation and an official denial are the marks of a cover-up, not a reckoning. Journalists heading to report the case were arrested. No senior figure in the state government answered for any of it.
pos: The state said the cremation respected the family's wishes and law-and-order needs, and ordered a probe.
alt: Dignity and consent for the family, an independent investigation, and consequences for officials who burned a body in secret.

title: Lakhimpur Kheri. A minister's son, farmers dead, no sacking

human.v: 8 killed, four of them farmers, one a journalist, and in the reprisal two BJP workers and a driver

cost.v: A Union minister's family accused of running down protesters, with no political consequence

what: An SUV ploughed into farmers protesting the farm laws in Lakhimpur Kheri, UP. The vehicle was tied to the convoy of the family of Union Minister of State for Home Ajay Mishra Teni, and his son Ashish Mishra was named prime accused.
dodge: With an FIR naming the minister's son, the Prime Minister still did not ask Ajay Mishra to go, and he stayed on in the Home Ministry, only to be re-nominated by the BJP for the 2024 election. It took the Supreme Court to get the accused arrested and his bail cancelled. Power closed ranks around its own.

ministers.r: Prime Minister who declined to act

pos: The minister and his son denied the son was present; the case is before the courts.
alleg: Ashish Mishra's role is before the courts. The accountability failure is that the minister paid no political price while the case ran.
alt: Step a minister aside pending a credible probe when his family is accused of killing protesters. That is the floor of ministerial responsibility.

title: The missing Census and the suppressed data

human.v: 1.4 billion citizens governed on a 2011 population base; welfare rolls frozen on stale numbers

cost.v: Crores potentially cut out of entitlements pegged to outdated data

what: The decennial Census, due in 2021, was postponed for years, the first such delay in 150 years, even as awkward datasets on jobs and consumption were delayed or held back.
dodge: Governing without current numbers is itself a way of dodging accountability, because it hides how many are poor, jobless or excluded. When surveys threw up inconvenient findings, they were buried or rubbished rather than released, so the government could never be measured against its own claims.
pos: The government cited the pandemic and administrative reasons for the delay.
alt: Run the Census, release datasets on a fixed public calendar, and wall the statistical system off from political convenience.

title: Agnipath. Recruitment overhaul over youth objections

human.v: Lakhs of aspirants affected; only ~25% of 'Agniveers' to be kept on after four years

cost.v: Public property torched in nationwide protests; trains burned

what: A scheme that replaced permanent military recruitment with four-year 'Agniveer' contracts, most of whom leave with no pension.
dodge: Announced with no real consultation and forced through despite violent protests, the core grievances of job security and veteran status were met with cosmetic tweaks, not a rethink or a pause to build consent.
pos: The government says Agnipath builds a younger force and gives youth skills and a stipend.
alt: Consult veterans and aspirants, pilot before a national rollout, and confront pension and post-service security head-on.

title: The ED as a political weapon (alleged)

human.v: Opposition leaders arrested and jailed for long spells before any conviction

cost.v: A watchdog widely accused of working to a political calendar

what: The Enforcement Directorate's powers under the money-laundering law were widened and, after a 2022 Supreme Court ruling, hardened, with a near-impossible bail bar and sweeping arrest and attachment powers.
dodge: Reporting and opposition tallies point to the overwhelming share of high-profile cases falling on opposition figures, often clustering around elections, while conviction rates stay strikingly low. Arrests and asset freezes land long before, and often without, any conviction, so the process itself becomes the punishment and the deterrent.
pos: The government insists the agencies act only on evidence and that courts have upheld the law.
alleg: The claim of election-timed, opposition-targeted misuse is a contested allegation from the opposition and some reporting; courts have upheld parts of the regime while flagging concerns in specific cases.
alt: Restore proportionate bail, require prior judicial sign-off for arrest and attachment, publish case data, and put an independent check on the agency.

title: Bilkis Bano. Gang-rape convicts freed, then sent back

human.v: 11 men convicted of gang rape and 7 murders, set free early, then ordered back to prison

cost.v: A survivor forced to fight the very state that released her attackers

what: On Independence Day 2022, the Gujarat government granted remission to 11 men serving life for the 2002 gang rape of Bilkis Bano and the murder of seven of her family, including a three-year-old. The freed men were garlanded.
dodge: The remission panel reportedly included ruling-party office-bearers, and the release cut against a 2014 central policy barring remission for rape and murder. In 2024 the Supreme Court quashed it, finding Gujarat had usurped jurisdiction and acted in tandem with the convicts. A court, not a conscience, restored the sentence.
pos: The state said it applied its 1992 remission policy after the men had served over 15 years.
alt: No early release for gang rape and murder, no political hands on remission panels, and respect for the survivor's right to be heard.

title: Morbi bridge collapse. 135+ dead, no political head rolled

human.v: 135 to 141 killed, including 47 children; 50+ injured

cost.v: A ₹2 cr maintenance contract on which barely ₹12 lakh was reportedly spent before reopening

what: A colonial-era suspension bridge, reopened after repairs with no fitness certificate and no load test, snapped over the Machchhu river days later and dropped a festival crowd into the water.
dodge: An SIT held the private operator and municipal officials responsible; the operator's MD was arrested and an official suspended. But not one BJP minister in the state government that oversaw the civic body resigned or was held to account, and victims were still fighting for compensation years later.
pos: The state pointed to the operator's negligence and to the SIT and court process.
alt: Political accountability alongside criminal, a clear chain of responsibility from contractor to civic body to minister, and fast, guaranteed compensation.

title: Joshimath. A Himalayan town sinking

human.v: Hundreds of families evacuated as homes cracked and streets buckled

cost.v: A whole town destabilised, linked to hydro and highway projects

what: The pilgrimage town of Joshimath in Uttarakhand began sinking in early 2023, with cracks tearing through hundreds of buildings and residents forced out.
dodge: Experts had warned for decades that the fragile slope could not carry heavy construction, and pointed to hydro-power tunnelling and the Char Dham road widening. Those warnings were overridden in the rush to build, and when the town cracked, the state managed the optics more than the causes.
pos: The government said it was rehabilitating residents and studying the causes.
alt: Heed the geology, halt reckless Himalayan construction, and hold accountable those who cleared projects against expert advice.

title: Manipur. A state on fire, and months of silence

human.v: ~258 killed, 60,000+ displaced, 1,000+ injured, thousands of homes and religious sites burned

cost.v: A state cleaved in two by ethnicity; long internet blackouts and economic collapse

what: Ethnic violence between Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities erupted in May 2023 and ground on for nearly two years, with reports of state complicity and horrific gender-based violence.
dodge: The Prime Minister stayed publicly silent for around three months and stayed away far longer. The BJP Chief Minister clung on through some 20 months of continuous killing, resigning only in 2025 under a looming no-confidence motion, after which rights groups noted that accountability for the violence still had not come. A burning state was treated as an inconvenience to be managed.
pos: The government cited security operations, central forces and later President's Rule, and blamed cross-border factors.
alleg: Allegations of state complicity, including an audio clip attributed to the CM, went to the Supreme Court for forensic examination and remain contested and under process.
alt: Swift accountability at the top, an independent inquiry into complicity, protection and return of the displaced, and justice for gender-based crimes.

title: ₹2,000 note withdrawn. A quiet admission

human.v: Ordinary cash users sent back to bank queues to exchange the note

cost.v: The note introduced in the 2016 note-ban, quietly withdrawn seven years on

what: The RBI announced the withdrawal of the ₹2,000 note, the very denomination introduced during the 2016 demonetisation as its supposed replacement currency.
dodge: Pulling the note was a tacit confession that a centrepiece of the 2016 upheaval had not worked as promised. It came with no acknowledgement of that failure and no account of the disruption both exercises caused.
pos: The government and RBI called it routine currency management under a clean-note policy.
alt: Level with the public about what the 2016 note-ban did and did not achieve, instead of unwinding it in silence.

title: Balasore train disaster. The resignation that never came

human.v: ~290+ killed and 1,000+ injured in one of India's worst rail crashes

cost.v: Hard questions over safety-fund use and vacancies in safety-critical posts

what: A signalling failure caused a three-train collision near Balasore, Odisha, the deadliest Indian rail accident in decades.
dodge: With scrutiny falling on deferred safety spending and unfilled safety-critical vacancies, the Railways Minister offered words of accountability but did not resign, and the systemic questions were folded into a technical inquiry rather than a political reckoning.
pos: The government pointed to the inquiry and to record investment in rail safety and modernisation.
alt: Publish safety-fund use and vacancy data, close the signalling-integrity gaps, and treat the deadliest crash in decades as a matter of ministerial responsibility.

title: Silkyara tunnel. 41 men trapped by a rushed project

human.v: 41 workers trapped for 17 days inside a collapsed Char Dham tunnel; all rescued

cost.v: A marquee project with no working escape passage when it caved

what: Part of the Silkyara tunnel on the flagship Char Dham highway in Uttarakhand collapsed, trapping 41 workers for 17 days until a dramatic manual rescue freed them.
dodge: The tunnel had no completed escape passage despite the requirement, and the wider Char Dham project had long faced warnings about cutting fragile Himalayan slopes and thin environmental scrutiny. The near-tragedy was celebrated as a rescue, while the questions of why it happened went unanswered.
pos: The government hailed the rescue and ordered a safety audit of tunnels under construction.
alt: Build the mandated escape routes first, respect Himalayan geology and environmental review, and hold the project accountable for the near-disaster, not just praised for the rescue.

title: Election Commission law. The Chief Justice written out

human.v: Every voter relying on a neutral referee for the vote

cost.v: A selection panel re-tilted toward the government of the day

what: A new law fixed the panel that appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners as the Prime Minister, a Union minister and the Leader of the Opposition, removing the Chief Justice of India, whom the Supreme Court had just placed on it.
dodge: Months after the Court tried to insulate the poll body by adding the Chief Justice, Parliament legislated the Chief Justice back out, handing the ruling side a built-in majority in choosing the referee of its own elections. The umpire's independence was diluted by law, and the government's convenience was the obvious winner.
pos: The government said Parliament, not the judiciary, is entitled to design the appointment process.
alt: A genuinely independent selection panel, including the judiciary or another non-partisan check, so the referee does not answer to one team.

title: Chandigarh mayor poll. Ballots defaced on camera

human.v: An entire electorate's verdict, nearly stolen by one official

cost.v: 8 opposition votes wrongly voided to hand the seat to the ruling party

what: In the Chandigarh mayoral election the returning officer declared eight votes of the opposition INDIA bloc invalid, handing the seat to the BJP candidate, while a video showed him defacing ballots and glancing at the camera.
dodge: Caught on tape, the officer's conduct was defended in court by the government's own law officer. The Supreme Court called it a murder of democracy, said the officer should be prosecuted, and took the rare step of counting the voided votes itself to declare the rightful winner, delivering the accountability the system had refused.
pos: The officer first claimed the ballots were already defaced; the Supreme Court rejected this after watching the video.
alt: Independent, videographed election administration with instant consequences for tampering, not a top court forced to referee a rigged municipal vote.

sources.label: RO to be prosecuted (Bar and Bench)

title: NEET / NTA 2024. The paper-leak collapse

human.v: ~2.4 million (24 lakh) NEET candidates thrown into chaos; careers and a year on the line

cost.v: Re-tests, coaching costs and lost time across a multi-thousand-crore exam economy

what: India's medical entrance exam was hit by a paper leak traced to Bihar and a grace-marks fiasco that produced an impossible cluster of perfect scores, with the CBI arresting a leak network.
dodge: The NTA first branded the leak reports baseless, then the government sacked the agency's chief, formed a committee and passed an anti-cheating law, while the Education Minister carried no personal accountability at all. The fix did not hold, as 2026 would prove.
pos: The government cites the CBI probe, the sacked chief, a reform committee and a new anti-cheating Act.
alt: Own it at the top and rebuild the testing agency end to end, so 2.4 million futures do not hinge on a leaky trunk.

title: Showcase infrastructure that failed on schedule

human.v: A death at a collapsing airport canopy; countless citizens on unsafe new-built roads and bridges

cost.v: Crores in flagship projects, such as a ~₹1,800 cr temple complex, leaking or caving within months

what: A run of prestige projects failed soon after grand inaugurations. New Ayodhya roads caved and the temple sanctum leaked in the first rains, a Delhi airport canopy collapsed and killed a man, and newly built bridges and airport roofs failed across states.
dodge: Each failure was blamed on unprecedented rain or a nameless contractor and quietly patched. Inaugurate with fanfare, fail within months, hold no one to account. It is the signature of a state that rewards the ribbon-cutting and ignores the engineering.
pos: Authorities blamed exceptional weather and promised swift repairs and inquiries.
alt: Publish quality audits and third-party structural certification before inauguration, and hold agencies, not the weather, to account when showcase projects fail.

title: Ken-Betwa river link. A tiger reserve for a headline

human.v: ~7,000 mostly tribal families across 21 to 22 villages to lose land and homes

cost.v: ₹44,605 cr; up to 2 to 4 million trees felled; core Panna Tiger Reserve submerged

what: The Ken-Betwa river-linking project, approved in 2021 and launched by the Prime Minister in December 2024, will dam the Ken to send water to the Betwa, submerging around 9,000 hectares, including roughly 5,800 hectares of the core of the Panna Tiger Reserve.
dodge: The Supreme Court's own Central Empowered Committee warned of irreversible damage, and experts called it a designed disaster, yet it was pushed through as a showpiece for river-linking. Madhya Pradesh bears the ecological and human cost, thousands of tribal families lose ancestral land, and the environmental warnings were simply overruled.
pos: The government says the project will bring water to drought-hit Bundelkhand and irrigate lakhs of hectares.
alt: Weigh irreversible tiger-habitat and forest loss honestly, exhaust local water options first, and secure genuine, informed consent from displaced tribal communities.

title: E20 petrol. No fuel choice, no compensation
stamp: Consumers left to absorb the cost

human.v: Millions of pre-2023 vehicle owners; ~28% report unusual wear, ~2 in 3 report lower mileage

cost.v: 2 to 5% mileage loss nationwide, plus repair bills and rejected insurance claims

what: India completed a nationwide switch to 20 percent ethanol-blended petrol six years ahead of target, making E20 effectively the only fuel at pumps, with no unblended option and no price difference.
dodge: Owners of older vehicles never designed for E20 report falling mileage, corrosion and repair costs, yet were given no choice, no labelling and no compensation. The government's answer was that the fuel is safe, and the Supreme Court declined to step in, so consumers were left to swallow a cost the state imposed on them.
pos: The ministry says E20 cuts crude imports and emissions, helps farmers, and passed extensive compatibility testing.
alt: Offer a labelled, unblended choice at the pump as the US and EU do, and compensate or grandfather owners of vehicles never built for E20.

sources.label: Owner anger, questions for govt (Al Jazeera)

title: NEET 2026. The 'fixed' exam leaks all over again

human.v: ~2.27 million aspirants; the exam cancelled nine days after it was held

cost.v: Another lost year for a generation of medical hopefuls; a nation of parents back on edge

what: Two years after the 2024 debacle and a fanfare of reforms, GPS-tracked papers, jammers and a new anti-cheating law, NEET-UG 2026 was cancelled on 12 May after a circulating guess paper was found to overlap heavily with the real exam. The CBI moved in and arrests followed.
dodge: The repeat laid the 2024 fixes bare as theatre. The same agency, the same leak, the same script of a sacked official and a fresh committee. No minister has owned the second collapse, even as it fed a nationwide youth protest movement over exam integrity and jobs. The message to 2.27 million young people was that their futures are expendable.
pos: The government again pointed to the CBI probe, the arrests and a scheduled re-examination.
alt: Treat a second collapse as a resignation-level failure and rebuild exam security under genuinely independent oversight, not another in-house committee.

title: The children the exam system killed

human.v: ~12 to 14 student deaths reported around the 2026 NEET leak and forced re-exam; scores more in prior years

cost.v: A generation taught that a rigged system holds their lives cheap

what: After the 2026 NEET leak, cancellation and a stressful forced re-examination, around a dozen students were reported to have died by suicide amid the anguish, part of a documented pattern of exam-linked student deaths over several years.
dodge: Asked in Parliament about student suicides in the coaching-and-exam pipeline, the government replied that it maintains no such data, the same refusal to count that it deployed on migrants and on the oxygen dead. A system that leaks papers, cancels exams and then cannot even be bothered to count the young lives lost is a system that has stopped caring who it breaks.
pos: The government says education is largely a state subject and that it has moved to ease exam pressure and add counselling.
alt: Count and publish the deaths, fix exam integrity and scheduling, fund real student mental-health support, and treat each loss as a failure of the state, not a statistic to avoid.

title: The falling rupee. The yardstick they buried

human.v: Costlier fuel, imports, foreign study and medicine for every household

cost.v: From ~₹59 per dollar in May 2014 to a record ~₹96.8 in May 2026

what: The rupee slid to a series of record lows through 2026, touching around 96.8 to the US dollar, having stood near 59 when this government took office in 2014.
dodge: The party that once brandished a falling rupee as proof of the previous government's weakness has presided over a far steeper slide, and now waves it away as the work of global forces alone. Whatever the mix of causes, the silence on its own former yardstick is its own small act of unaccountability.
pos: The government points, with some justification, to a strong dollar, high oil prices, US tariffs and global capital flows.
alt: Apply one honest standard over time, name the real causes without spin, and stop treating a currency as a scoreboard only when it suits.

title: Ram Mandir donation theft. Faith, cash and deleted tape

human.v: Crores in offerings from ordinary devotees, allegedly siphoned by insiders

cost.v: Claims ranged from ₹5 to 7.5 cr to media estimates topping ₹200 cr missing

what: An alleged racket saw daily cash offerings at the Ayodhya Ram temple siphoned off by insiders. A state SIT found suspicious pilferage on camera, staff appointed on the recommendation of trust officials, and CCTV footage allegedly deleted despite audit warnings to keep long backups.
dodge: A trust the government itself says is not answerable to it, stuffed with figures from the ruling ecosystem, presided over faith money vanishing while cameras were wiped and warnings ignored. The response was cosmetic. Key office-bearers resigned on moral grounds yet stayed on as trust members, in what critics bluntly called an eyewash, with no wider independent inquiry.

ministers.n: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust
ministers.r: A trust, not a govt body, but tied to the ruling ecosystem

pos: Trust officials said they themselves sought the SIT probe and were unaware of the alleged theft.
alleg: The theft and the scale of missing funds are under SIT investigation and not yet proven; figures are contested media and official estimates.
alt: An independent audit and inquiry, full public accounts for a trust built on public devotion, real accountability rather than resignations that change nothing, and transparency the government cannot disclaim.

title: Delhi-Dehradun Expressway. Potholes in ten weeks

human.v: Motorists on a flagship expressway hit by tyre damage on a caved stretch

cost.v: A marquee highway degrading within roughly 10 weeks of its opening

what: About two and a half months after its high-profile opening, a stretch of the new Delhi-Dehradun Expressway near Shamli developed deep potholes after heavy rain, with motorists reportedly suffering tyre damage.
dodge: The highways authority blamed a blocked culvert and local land issues, suspended some officials and ordered an inquiry, the now-familiar loop of blame the rain, patch the hole, move on. Opposition demands for accountability on construction quality met the usual reassurance that prompt action had been taken.
pos: The authority said the damage was from waterlogging due to a blocked culvert, was fixed quickly, and officials were suspended pending inquiry.
alt: Independent quality audits and enforceable contractor warranties for flagship highways, with the findings published, not another inquiry that quietly closes.

title: Adani-Hindenburg. And the JPC that was refused

human.v: Retail investors and LIC and SBI stakeholders exposed to the 2023 market rout

cost.v: Tens of billions of dollars in market value wiped out in the 2023 sell-off (contested cause)

what: A short-seller's report accused the Adani Group, a conglomerate widely seen as close to the government, of stock manipulation and accounting fraud, triggering a huge sell-off.
dodge: With public-sector LIC and SBI exposed, the opposition demanded a Joint Parliamentary Committee to examine the ties between political power and corporate rise. The government refused, leaving the proximity questions to a narrow regulatory process rather than open parliamentary scrutiny.

ministers.r: Oversight of markets and PSU exposure

pos: The government denied favouritism; an SC-appointed panel found no conclusive regulatory failure, and SEBI continued its probe.
alleg: The manipulation and crony-capitalism claims are allegations, denied by the group and not established by courts. The accountability point is the refusal of independent parliamentary scrutiny.
alt: Grant a JPC or an equivalent independent probe, and ring-fence public financial institutions from politically sensitive exposures.

title: Wrestlers' protest. A ruling-party MP shielded

human.v: Olympic medallists among the complainants; a minor among the original accusers

cost.v: India's most decorated wrestlers dragged from a protest and booked

what: Top wrestlers, including Olympic medallists, sat in at Jantar Mantar accusing the Wrestling Federation chief and six-time BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexually harassing female athletes.
dodge: Police registered cases only after the Supreme Court intervened. As the new Parliament was inaugurated, the protesting wrestlers were detained, dragged away and later booked. The accused MP was never arrested. The state policed the accusers and protected the accused, and the Prime Minister said nothing.
pos: Singh denied all allegations; the government said the law was taking its course and a chargesheet was filed.
alleg: The harassment allegations are before the courts. The accountability failure is the delay in registering cases and the policing of the complainants.
alt: Prompt, unbiased investigation of complaints against the powerful, protection for complainants, and no shielding of an accused because he holds a party seat.

title: 'Bulldozer justice'. Punishment by demolition

human.v: Homes and shops of the merely accused, often Muslim, often poor, flattened without a trial

cost.v: SC later ordered ₹60 lakh restitution for six wrongly-demolished Prayagraj families

what: Several BJP-run states demolished the homes of people merely accused of crimes or of joining protests, staging the bulldozer as instant justice.
dodge: For years the practice ran as a spectacle of power, punishing whole families before any court had ruled. Only in November 2024 did the Supreme Court declare punitive demolitions unconstitutional, the executive cannot become a judge, and make officials personally liable. Accountability came from the bench, never from the governments that drove the bulldozer.

ministers.n: BJP state governments (UP, MP, Rajasthan and others)

pos: States said they demolished only illegal structures under municipal law, not as punishment.
alt: Due process for every demolition, notice, hearing and appeal, and personal liability for officials who bulldoze homes as punishment.

title: CAA. Religion written into citizenship
stamp: Contested. Under challenge in the SC.

human.v: The first religion test in Indian citizenship; anti-CAA protests left 25+ dead, over 20 of them in Uttar Pradesh

cost.v: The stake is the secular basis of Indian citizenship, not a rupee figure

what: The Citizenship Amendment Act amended the 1955 law to fast-track citizenship for non-Muslim migrants, Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian, who entered from Pakistan, Bangladesh or Afghanistan before 31 December 2014. For the first time in independent India, religion became a criterion in naturalisation. The rules were notified in March 2024, more than four years later, just before the general election.
dodge: The law was pushed through amid the largest protests in years, met with police crackdowns and, in places, deadly violence, and paired with talk of a nationwide NRC that raised the spectre of a documentation trap with a religious escape hatch open to some communities and shut to Muslims. The government has faced no reckoning for the protest deaths, sat on the rules for over four years and then rushed them out on the eve of an election, and the constitutional questions remain unresolved in court while the divisions it opened harden.
pos: The government says the law is purely humanitarian, offers refuge to persecuted minorities, takes away no Indian's citizenship, and that mere under-inclusion of a group is no ground to strike a law down.
alleg: The claim that the CAA is unconstitutional and discriminates on religion, violating Articles 14 and 21, is the case made by around 230 petitioners and is pending before the Supreme Court, which has declined to stay the law and set final hearings for 2026. It has not been adjudicated.
alt: A religion-neutral asylum and refugee framework that shelters anyone facing persecution on the evidence of their plight, not the label of their faith, meeting the humanitarian aim without dividing citizenship along sectarian lines.

sources.label: SC to hear ~200 petitions, final hearings 2026

date: Mallya fled 2016. PNB scam broke Feb 2018.
title: The fugitives who fled with public money

human.v: State-owned banks and, through them, the taxpayer left holding thousands of crore

cost.v: PNB fraud ~₹13,000 to 14,500 cr; 15 declared fugitive offenders owe banks ~₹58,000 cr, of which only ~₹19,000 cr recovered

what: Diamond tycoons Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi allegedly defrauded state-owned Punjab National Bank of around ₹13,000 to 14,500 crore through fake Letters of Undertaking, the biggest banking fraud in Indian history, while liquor baron Vijay Mallya defaulted on over ₹9,000 crore owed by his airline. All of them left the country before or just as the cases broke.
dodge: Each high-profile accused slipped out of India on the government's watch, Mallya in 2016, and Nirav Modi in early 2018, weeks before the PNB fraud went public and days after he was photographed among industrialists at a Davos event with the Prime Minister. Years of assurances that they would be brought back have produced drawn-out extradition battles and only a fraction of the money recovered. The oversight failure that let them walk out of the country has answered to no one.
pos: The government points to the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act of 2018, ongoing extradition efforts, partial recoveries, and insists the defaulters remain liable.
alleg: The specific charges against the fugitives are before the courts in India and abroad. The accountability failure logged here is that they were able to flee at all, and that most of the public money is still unrecovered.
alt: A system that flags and stops large defaulters before they board a plane, genuinely fast extradition, and real recovery of public-bank money, rather than photo-ops and promises.

sources.label: 'All coming back to face law', said FM

title: ₹16 lakh crore written off. About 16% recovered.

human.v: Borne by public-sector banks and, ultimately, ordinary depositors and taxpayers

cost.v: ~₹16.35 to 16.61 lakh cr in bad loans written off since 2014; only about 16% recovered; roughly ₹9.26 lakh cr of it owed by big industry

what: Indian banks wrote off around ₹16.6 lakh crore in bad loans since 2014, according to RBI data given in an RTI reply and in Parliament, of which only about 16 percent has been recovered. The bulk, roughly ₹9 lakh crore, was owed by large industry and services.
dodge: Write-offs are, as the government insists, prudential accounting rather than formal waivers, yet the pattern is hard to stomach: colossal sums of public-bank money erased, overwhelmingly for big corporate borrowers, with recovery stuck near a sixth, while the borrowers' identities stay shielded under the RBI Act. The gulf between how gently large defaulters are treated and how hard small ones are chased has never been honestly answered.
pos: The government says write-offs are accounting measures, that borrowers remain liable, that recovery is an ongoing process, and that gross NPAs have since fallen to multi-year lows.
alt: Publish the names of big defaulters, pursue corporate recovery as relentlessly as small-borrower recovery, and account transparently for exactly what public money was lost and to whom.

sources.label: ₹16.61 lakh cr written off since 2014, 16% recovered
₹16.35 lakh cr over a decade, bulk to big industry

title: Assam NRC. ₹1,600 crore, then disowned
stamp: Built, then rejected by its own backers

human.v: 19,06,657 people left off the final list, their citizenship in limbo for years, disproportionately the poor and minorities

cost.v: ~₹1,600 cr and a decade of work by tens of thousands of officials, left unimplemented

what: The Supreme-Court-monitored National Register of Citizens in Assam, an exercise the BJP had long campaigned for, cost around ₹1,600 crore and a decade of work by tens of thousands of officials, and on 31 August 2019 excluded 19,06,657 people from the final list.
dodge: Having finally got the register it had demanded, the BJP-led state government and the Centre then refused to accept the result, alleging irregularities and seeking a re-verification, so the ₹1,600 crore exercise sits in limbo, unimplemented to this day. Rejection slips were never properly issued, and 19 lakh people were left in citizenship limbo with no closure. A vast public spend produced an outcome its own sponsors disowned the moment it did not suit them.
pos: The government says it sought re-verification to ensure a correct, error-free register, and that the whole process was monitored by the Supreme Court.
alt: Either stand by a court-monitored result or never launch a divisive, ruinously costly exercise you intend to disown, and give the 19 lakh excluded a fair, funded and time-bound path to be heard.

title: MP Chief Minister's family land, and a buried demand for a probe

human.v: Public trust in whether high office was used to profit from insider knowledge of land values

cost.v: Media put the alleged family-linked purchases at ~168 acres across ~137 parcels, worth ~₹45 cr, around Ujjain

what: Media reports in June 2026 alleged that firms and family members linked to Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav had acquired around 137 land parcels, roughly 168 acres, in and around Ujjain, concentrated in areas expected to rise in value from planned government infrastructure and development.
dodge: Whatever the truth of the purchases, the accountability question is what followed. The Chief Minister's office flatly denied that he or his wife had bought any land since he took office and called the reports misleading; the opposition demanded a judicial inquiry overseen by a sitting Supreme Court judge; and the government ordered no independent probe at all. A serious public allegation that office may have been used to gain from insider land values was met with a denial and a press line, not with the transparent, independent scrutiny that alone could clear it or prove it.
pos: The Chief Minister's Office denies that he or his wife purchased any land since he took office in December 2023, and calls the media reports misleading, promising a detailed response.
alleg: This is an unproven allegation based on media reporting and raised by opposition parties. It has not been tested by any court or independent inquiry, and the Chief Minister denies it. It is logged here for the accountability question it raises, not as an established fact.
alt: Refer serious conflict-of-interest allegations against those in office to a genuinely independent inquiry, and routinely publish the land and asset records of office-holders and their families, so the answer comes from scrutiny rather than a denial.

sources.label: CMO denies land deal; opposition seeks judicial probe

title: Ayushman Bharat. Dead patients 'treated', ghost phone numbers

human.v: The poor the scheme exists to cover, crowded out by fraud and, the audit found, sometimes still charged despite 'cashless' care

cost.v: ₹6.97 cr paid to 'treat' 3,446 patients already recorded as dead; up to 7.5 lakh beneficiaries on one phone number

what: The national auditor's 2023 performance audit of the Ayushman Bharat health-insurance scheme found up to 7.5 lakh beneficiaries registered against a single mobile number (9999999999), thousands registered against the same Aadhaar numbers, ₹6.97 crore paid for the treatment of 3,446 patients already recorded as dead, and tens of thousands of cases of one patient admitted to several hospitals at the same time.
dodge: This is not an opposition allegation but a finding of the Comptroller and Auditor General, tabled in Parliament. It points to large-scale leakage of public health money into fraud and ghost claims in a scheme meant for the poorest, with weak checks to stop it. The Health Ministry disputed how the mobile-number data should be read, but the core irregularities passed without any senior accountability or a full, public reckoning.
pos: The Health Ministry said mobile numbers play no role in verifying beneficiaries, that dummy numbers were used, and that AI-based checks and action on around 1.6 lakh flagged claims show fraud is being tackled.
alt: Close the ghost-beneficiary and dead-patient loopholes, publish the fraud and recovery data, and hold administrators accountable for public health money lost to leakage.

title: Namami Gange. Tens of thousands of crore, a river still filthy

human.v: The crores who live along a Ganga still carrying large volumes of untreated sewage

cost.v: Outlays of ₹20,000 cr and then ₹22,500 cr; over ₹13,000 cr spent; CAG flagged unspent funds and failing sewage plants

what: Launched in 2014 as the Prime Minister's flagship river-cleaning mission with an outlay of ₹20,000 crore, later topped up to ₹22,500 crore, Namami Gange has seen more than ₹13,000 crore spent, yet the Ganga still carries large volumes of untreated sewage.
dodge: Successive CAG audits have found underutilised funds, delayed and faulty sewage-treatment plants, and, in recent state audits, only a handful of plants meeting pollution norms, even as the government advertises the mission as a triumph. A decade and tens of thousands of crore later, the core promise of a clean Ganga is largely unmet, and the gap between the spending, the claims and the state of the river has never been honestly owned.
pos: The government says pollution has fallen, hundreds of sewage plants have been built or sanctioned, and wildlife such as river dolphins has returned.
alt: Tie funding to measurable water-quality outcomes, build and actually maintain the treatment plants, and publish honest, independent monitoring of the river against every rupee spent.
